serviceAvailable.description: Observations remain in the boundary DTO, but never grant or deny access.

Access2.description: Published booleans used by the interaction planner; no other server fields are retained.

AccessInteractionAction.description: Finite access intents; unknown wire actions fail before planning an effect.

AccessInteractionFacts.description: Published common decisions plus the user's local choices. This plans UI effects only; AccountAccessService still refreshes and validates mutations.

Context.description: Stored option maps and legacy mirrors are facts. Selection, defaults and updates have the same meaning on every binding.

Context2.description: Issuance allowance is distinct from the user's visible usage balance.

Context3.description: Device observations only. A bound session supplies profile freshness itself.

Document.description: Portable content only. No account identity, credentials, IO or migration.

Facts.description: Storage presence and local consent are facts, not financial authority.

Facts2.description: Device facts distinguish an OS-managed screen-off stop from an explicit timer.

Facts3.description: Native facts and the last instructed I/O step. The core owns sequencing, coalescing and the single follow-up budget; adapters only execute actions.

InputChanges.description: Current UI commands, not a decoder for historical preference documents.

Pass.description: IDs reference objects held by the native secure-storage port. Neither signed passes nor unblinding material crosses this business boundary.

ProfileActivity.description: One admission owner for profile work. Task handles remain runtime ports; neither Kotlin nor the desktop host chooses coalescing or follow-up work.

ProfileRefreshCadence.description: Volatile scheduling state, never an entitlement or persisted tariff clock. Hosts supply monotonic elapsed time. A ticket fences completion against a newer read or authoritative publication, even within the same account.

RequestSnapshot.description: No Debug implementation: a persisted request must never appear in logs. Binary fields keep the existing big-endian bytes, encoded without padding.

Settings.description: Preferences and OS observations, never credentials or account mutations.

State10.description: Recovery counts network opportunities, not inspections of a lease which is still waiting. The continuation is opaque to native I/O executors.

State11.description: An opaque, in-memory continuation. Native executors retain it unchanged; only this reducer owns budgets, coalescing, wakeups and completion ordering.

State2.description: Local library state. Account authority, styling enablement and IO are separate owners. Reading a view never rewrites the persisted strings or IDs.

State4.description: Process-local availability only. No account, credit, text, or wall clock.

Stored.description: OS storage facts include absent preferences on a fresh install. Reading them does not migrate or rewrite storage.

StreamState.description: Counts and flags only. The OS adapter owns any buffered transcript.

Style.description: Current portable preset shape, shared by local edits and content synchronization.

StyleWindowFacts.description: Server observations and content-free device accounting. This view cannot issue credits or authorize a request; the session and server retain that authority.

presentationAccess.description: Optional for admission-only callers; native display ports supply the server access DTO. Session-bound commands always replace it themselves.

SubscriptionInteractionAction.description: Subscription screen intents; only the server confirms payments.

Write.description: Both snapshots are durable: an uncertain write must not erase a later local revert.

description: Typed boundary for platform clients. No command can create a payment, grant access or bypass the account's explicitly confirmed mutation owner.
title: BusinessCommand
